items.q: Match the following insulin-resistance syndrome — 1) Type A 2) Type B 3) HAIR-AN 4) Donohue / Rabson-Mendenhall … A) Defective insulin receptor gene B) Anti-insulin-receptor autoantibodies C) Hyperandrogenism, IR, acanthosis D) Severe insulin-receptor mutations with childhood mortality
items.exp: Type A insulin-resistance is due to insulin-receptor gene mutations; Type B is autoimmune with anti-receptor antibodies; HAIR-AN combines hyperandrogenism, IR and acanthosis nigricans; Donohue / Rabson-Mendenhall are severe receptor-mutation syndromes with childhood mortality. (Book p924)

items.q: A teenage girl has severe acanthosis nigricans, oligomenorrhoea and elevated testosterone with normal glucose initially but develops diabetes at 18. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance and acanthosis nigricans fit HAIR-AN. (Book p924)

items.q: Assess insulin-resistance syndromes: I Type A is autoimmune in origin. II Donohue syndrome presents with intrauterine growth restriction.
items.exp: Type A is genetic (receptor mutations), Type B is autoimmune; Donohue syndrome includes intrauterine growth restriction and severe neonatal features. (Book p924)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a MODY subtype?
items.exp: Type A insulin-resistance is a receptor disorder, not a MODY subtype; the others are common MODY subtypes. (Book p924)

items.q: Donohue and Rabson-Mendenhall syndromes are caused by mutations in the ___ gene.
items.exp: Both are due to severe insulin-receptor mutations (INSR). (Book p924)

items.q: Match the following MODY subtype to its genetic defect — 1) MODY 2 2) MODY 3 3) MODY 5 (HNF1B) … A) Glucokinase (GCK) B) HNF1A transcription factor C) HNF1B with renal cysts
items.exp: MODY 2 is GCK; MODY 3 is HNF1A; MODY 5 is HNF1B with renal cysts and genital tract anomalies. (Book p924)

items.q: A 22-year-old with mild hyperglycaemia, family history of mild diabetes, and renal cysts on ultrasound is most likely to have:
items.exp: MODY 5 (HNF1B) is associated with renal cysts and genital tract malformations. (Book p924)

items.q: Assess MODY: I MODY is typically autosomal dominant. II MODY 3 often progresses and requires sulfonylurea therapy.
items.exp: MODY is autosomal dominant; HNF1A-MODY (MODY 3) is progressive and sulfonylurea-responsive. (Book p924)

items.q: Match the following neonatal diabetes gene — 1) KCNJ11 2) ABCC8 3) INS … A) K-ATP channel, sulfonylurea-responsive B) K-ATP channel, sulfonylurea-responsive C) Insulin gene mutation
items.exp: KCNJ11 and ABCC8 encode K-ATP channel subunits and are sulfonylurea-responsive; INS is the insulin gene mutation form. (Book p924)

items.q: A 6-week-old with persistent hyperglycaemia is found to have a KCNJ11 mutation. The most appropriate therapy is:
items.exp: KCNJ11 mutations causing neonatal diabetes are often successfully switched to high-dose sulfonylureas. (Book p924)

items.q: Gestational diabetes mellitus is screened at ___ weeks of gestation.
items.exp: Universal GDM screening is recommended at 24–28 weeks; high-risk women are screened earlier. (Book p924)

items.q: Assess GDM: I It is associated with increased future Type 2 diabetes risk. II First-line pharmacotherapy is glyburide.
items.exp: GDM raises future Type 2 diabetes risk; first-line pharmacotherapy is insulin, with metformin or glyburide as alternatives. (Book p924)
